title: AML / Reporting Thresholds

rows: 30 days of detection (60 if no suspect)
Reasonable belief of exploitation of specified adult
Up to 15 business days; +10 internal = 25; +30 if reported to regulator/court = 55 total

sections.heading: CTR — Critical Facts
items: CASH only — NOT checks, NOT wires (wires have separate $3,000 recordkeeping rule)
Aggregates multiple cash transactions same day, same customer
Need not be U.S. dollars
Penalties: up to $500,000 fine + 10 years prison
Filed by BD; goes to FinCEN (Treasury bureau, not DOJ)

sections.heading: SAR — Four Triggers ($5,000+)
items: 1) Funds derived from illegal activity
2) Designed to evade Bank Secrecy Act (e.g., structuring)
3) No business or apparent lawful purpose
4) Use of firm to facilitate criminal activity
CONFIDENTIAL — never tell the subject; if subpoenaed, refuse & notify FinCEN
NO dollar minimum for suspected terrorist financing

rows: Dirty cash enters financial system (deposits, buying chips, etc.)
Series of complex transactions to disguise source

sections.heading: Structuring (ILLEGAL)
items: Breaking cash deposits into amounts under $10,000 to evade CTR filing
Example: 25 deposits of $500 to pay for $12,500 trade = structuring
Triggers SAR filing; criminal offense even if underlying funds are legal

sections.heading: OFAC / SDN List
items: Office of Foreign Assets Control — division of TREASURY (not State, not DOJ)
SDN = Specially Designated Nationals — terrorists, narco-traffickers, sanctioned individuals/countries
All U.S. persons + entities PROHIBITED from doing business with anyone on SDN list
Check at account opening AND periodically thereafter
Assets of SDN persons are BLOCKED/FROZEN

sections.heading: AML Program — Required Elements (Rule 3310)
items: Designated AML Compliance Officer (need NOT be a registered principal)
Written policies & procedures
Ongoing employee training
Independent annual testing
Customer Identification Program (CIP) — verify ID before opening account

sections.heading: FINRA Rule 3220 — Gifts & Gratuities
items: $100 max per person, per year, to employees of other member firms
Applies to business-related gifts; personal gifts (weddings, etc.) generally excluded
Must log all gifts given/received
Promotional items <$50 with firm logo typically excluded
Bereavement gifts excluded
Does NOT cap business entertainment (meals/events) if rep is present and reasonable

sections.heading: FinCEN at a Glance
items: Bureau of U.S. TREASURY (not DOJ, not SEC)
Intelligence agency — NO law-enforcement arm
Collects CTRs, SARs to combat money laundering & terrorist financing

common_traps: CTR is CASH ONLY — checks and wire transfers do NOT trigger a CTR (wires have their own $3,000 recordkeeping rule).
Mixing up deadlines: CTR = 15 days, SAR = 30 days. Don't flip them.
SAR has NO dollar minimum for suspected terrorist financing — the $5,000 threshold does not apply.
OFAC is part of TREASURY, not Justice or State Department. FinCEN is also Treasury.
PLACEMENT (not layering) is the stage most susceptible to detection — cash entering the system is the easiest red flag.
Rule 3220 gift limit is $100 per person PER YEAR — not per gift, not per occasion.
